transcript: Ragtime is maybe my favorite score of all time so for me to call this New York City Center production highly anticipated would have been a complete understatement. And I'm pleased to report that it did not disappoint. First staged in New York in 1998, this is a huge musical about three groups of people in and around New York at the turn of the 20th century. It is a complicated, searing, hopeful, and heartbreaking portrait of America, and it continues to be a beloved and relevant show in 2024. With this being a limited run and City Center’s gala presentation, the staging is simple and the production value is pretty modest. But in every other sense, the show is grand: A dense, three-hour story of epic proportions, a juggernaut score played to the nines by a magnificent 28-piece orchestra, and stunning vocal performances by a roof-raising, all-star cast. It's very much an ensemble show, but if you were to identify a centerpiece, it would be Joshua Henry at the best he's ever been as Coalhouse. He delivers a ferociously passionate and moving performance, brought to new heights by his almost indescribably rich voice. Caissie Levy and Brandon Uranowitz as Mother and Tateh knock their roles out of the park as well. And of course the supporting cast is chock-full of wonders with Nichelle Lewis, Ben Levi Ross, and Shaina Taub giving particularly memorable performances in my opinion. To quell any rumours of frivolous exaggeration, I'll just say that this was one of my favourite productions I've seen all year and it is not to be missed. The hype is real and I think the ticket sales are reflecting that. Hopefully a Broadway transfer is imminent since getting an affordable seat is becoming difficult and this production is closing on November 10th. With that, another program for my collection.
